text:
Ottawa arrives in Pittsburgh on a good run. The Senators are 3-1-1 in their last five, and on Wednesday they beat Colorado 4-3 in overtime after trailing in the third period, with Shane Pinto scoring the winner. They're missing Nick Cousins, Andre Burakovsky and Warren Foegele, plus William Eklund, with Tim Stützle now on Eklund's old line beside Dylan Cozens and Fabian Zetterlund. The Penguins are home after a three-game road trip, coming off a shootout win in San Jose, but they're 2-3-0 in their last five and without Bryan Rust, with Evgeni Malkin moving next to Sidney Crosby and Rickard Rakell in his place.

Our numbers see little between them: each team has taken 52% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) at five on five, and we have the game at 3.2 to 3.13 for Ottawa. Pittsburgh gives up more chances, 3.41 expected goals per 60 against Ottawa's 2.98, and Ottawa takes 4.7 penalties a game. Both projected goalies have struggled. Samuel Ersson is 1.1 goals worse than expected this season, and Arturs Silovs is 2.6 worse, after finishing last season 12.8 below.

In the Ottawa lineup, we have Stützle at 35% to score and 76% for a point. Philip Tomasino, back in Pittsburgh for the first time since leaving the Penguins, is one point from 100 career points. For Pittsburgh, Crosby is at 34% to score. Our under-the-radar pick is Zetterlund, a third-liner with 3.2 expected goals in his last 10 games and six high-danger shots, at 19% to score. He's a player to watch, not a lock.
